| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **8.1.4** | [GRAMMAR] Verify that the application can detect and alert on abnormal numbers of requests, such as by IP, user, total per hour or day, or whatever makes sense for the application. | 2 | 770 |

I have opened the discussion for the requirement previously in #1272, but it did not get addressed back then.

Problems with the requirement:

  * it is in "V8 Data Protection > V8.1 General Data Protection", but it is "detecting a security event" (V7) when "anti-automation defense triggers" (V11)
  * Is "alerting" within the scope of ASVS? (#2630)

I think this is pure security event detection and belongs to "V7.2 Security Events". Otherwise, I can say, that defense against SQL injection is also for general data protection and everything belongs to V8.1.

comments.body:
The content is also quite close to:

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **7.2.4** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 11.1.7] Verify that the application monitors for unusual events or activity from a business logic perspective. | 2 | 754 |

I think those can be merged.

ping @tghosth

How about:

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **7.2.4** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 11.1.7, MERGED FROM 8.1.4] Verify that the application can detect and alert on unusual activity, including business logic anomalies and abnormal or excessive request patterns. | 2 | 754 |

I would propose:

"_[MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 11.1.7, MERGED FROM 8.1.4] Verify that the application can detect and log unusual activity, including business logic anomalies and abnormal or excessive request patterns, such as by IP, user, total per hour or day, or whatever makes sense for the application._"

You can see these changes in a commit here:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/2646/files
Let's get rid of "or whatever makes sense for the application." or replace it with something "based on documented limits".
The wording is ok but I'm confused what is the PR-logic used there?
This latest change works for me.
